title: Axios Interview: AI Chip Squeeze Less a One-Off; Further Hikes Hinge on Whether Shocks Fade
summary: Daly's first read after the September hike (press coverage only, an Axios interview) and the clearest hawkish shift in her corpus: in Tokyo (Aug 5) she backed the July hold and saw 'good reasons' the supply shocks would not last; now she calls the September hike 'completely necessary' because 'inflation risks have gone up.' The new element is AI: drawing on Silicon Valley contacts (forward contracts for memory chips, products re-engineered to use fewer chips), she sees AI-driven chip pressure as 'less ... a one-off' with relief 'probably further out' than the one-to-three-year horizon over which the Fed normally looks through shocks, and a risk of spillover into autos and other goods. Further hikes are explicitly conditional: if tariffs, oil and AI behave as conventional temporary shocks 'we may not need more,' a scenario she still gives 'some probability,' but if they compound or last longer (e.g. a second round of tariffs) the period of pressure extends. She keeps a dual-mandate caveat (the FOMC is 'not going to lose track of the labor market') and notes tightening still works through the rate-sensitive economy even if hyperscalers are not very rate-sensitive. Net: from a patient hold to backing the hike with a conditional lean toward more, still short of the hawks who see policy 'out of position'; she is NOT a 2026 voter.

key_quotes.quote: It seemed completely necessary at this juncture to respond to the fact that inflation risks have gone up.
key_quotes.context: On the September hike, which she was 'very supportive' of; in August she backed the hold

key_quotes.quote: This is probably further out before we get relief.
key_quotes.context: AI-driven chip/tech price pressure vs the one-to-three-year horizon over which the Fed usually looks through shocks

key_quotes.quote: then we may not need more. And I still have some probability on that.
key_quotes.context: If tariffs, oil and AI prove conventional temporary shocks; if they compound or last longer, more may be needed

key_quotes.quote: I do think tightening policy has an effect on the outlook for inflation
key_quotes.context: Even though hyperscalers are not very rate-sensitive, other AI investors and the broader economy are
